what: The heuristic precomputes a directed routing-cost matrix from grounded visit, return-to-depot, and visit-via-depot operator costs. It also discovers visited/location fact references and, where available, load, vehicles, capacity, max-vehicles, and customer demands from numeric variables and assignment effects. At evaluation time it reads the current state, finds the current location and unvisited customers, then greedily builds a capacity-aware nearest-neighbor route from the current vehicle. It uses direct visit costs when load permits, otherwise splits a new route through the depot using via-depot costs, adds the final return-to-depot cost, and applies a penalty when the simulated number of extra routes exceeds the available vehicle limit.
why: The design follows the structure of the CVRP actions: direct customer-to-customer moves are cheap, and route splits are modeled by visit-via-depot costs. Greedy nearest-neighbor over unvisited customers using the actual directed cost matrix is efficient and gives a state-dependent estimate of the remaining route length, while optional demand/capacity information allows the heuristic to account for route splits instead of assuming a single route. This keeps evaluation cheap (quadratic in the number of unvisited customers) and generalizes because all task-dependent information is discovered from operator and fact names and numeric variables, with no hardcoded instance values.
